Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 109, verses 1–3:

Surat al-Kafirun (The Disbelievers) is Meccan [[Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "Surat (Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun) was revealed in Mecca." See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/654.]] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful (﷽)

* *

﴿Say: O you who disbelieve,﴾ to the end of the surah.

It was revealed concerning a group of the Quraysh, among them: al-Harith ibn Qays al-Sahmi, al-'As ibn Wa'il, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, [al-Aswad] [[In "A" it reads al-Asad; the correct reading is what has been established.]] ibn 'Abd Yaghuth, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib ibn Asad, [202/b] and Umayya ibn Khalaf. They said: "O Muhammad, [come and follow] [[In "A" it reads: "Hal tattabi'" (will you follow).]] our religion and we will follow your religion; you will share with us in our whole affair. You worship our gods for a year and we will worship your God for a year. If what you have brought is better, we will have shared with you in it and taken our portion of it, and if what is in our hands is better, you will have shared with us in our affair and taken your portion of it." He said: "I seek refuge in Allah from associating anything else with Him." They said: "Then touch some of our gods, and we will believe you and worship your God." He said: "Wait until I see what comes from my Lord." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "Say: O you who disbelieve," to the end of the surah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out in the morning to the Sacred Mosque, where the chiefs of the Quraysh were present, and he stood over their heads and recited it to them until he finished the surah. They then despaired of him, harmed him and his companions. [[Narrated by Ibn Ishaq; Sirat Ibn Hisham: 1/362. See also al-Tabari: 30/331; Ibn Kathir: 4/561; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 543. The Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) said in al-Fath: 8/333: Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Cease from our gods, and do not mention them with evil; if you do not, then worship our gods for a year and we will worship your God for a year," and so it was revealed. Its chain contains Abu Khalaf 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa, who is weak.]]

The meaning of the verse: ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾ at present, ﴿nor do you worship what I worship﴾ at present,

ā﻿Here is the translation:

﴿Nor am I going to worship what you worship﴾ — in the future tense; ﴿nor are you going to worship what I worship﴾ — in the future tense [[See: al-Bukhari, 8/733, the chapter heading.]].

This is an address to those who, in God's knowledge, were already destined not to believe.

As for His saying "mā a'budu" (what I worship), it means "man a'budu" (whom I worship), but it was stated in this form to correspond with "mā ta'budūn" (what you worship).

As for the repetition: most of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said that the Qur'an was revealed in the language of the Arabs and according to the conventions of their speech, and among their methods is repetition, intended for emphasis and clarification, just as among their methods is brevity, intended for lightness and conciseness.

Al-Qutaybi said: the repetition of the speech is for the repetition of the occasion, because they said: "If you wish that we enter your religion for one year, then enter our religion for one year." So this surah was revealed.

﴿To you is your religion﴾ — that is, polytheism; ﴿and to me is my religion﴾ [[al-Farra' said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (3/297): "He did not say 'dini' (my religion) because the verse-endings are with a nun, so the yā' was dropped, as in 'yahdin' and 'yashfin'."]] — that is, Islam. Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Hafs read "wa-liya" with a fatha on the yā', and the others read it with a sukun on it. [[The words in brackets are omitted from manuscript "B". As for his saying "this verse is abrogated by the verse of the sword": this is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, but there is no contradiction between this verse and the verse of the sword, so there is no room for saying it is abrogated, because reconciling the two is possible, and one does not resort to abrogation except when reconciling the two verses is impossible. The meaning of the verse is: "to you is your religion" — so you will never abandon it, for God has sealed your hearts; "and to me is my religion" — which I will never abandon. This is because the polytheists, as mentioned earlier, asked the Messenger ﷺ to worship their gods for one year and they would worship his God for one year, so the surah was revealed to clarify their state and to despair the Messenger ﷺ of the faith of specific individuals and to stop him hoping for their faith. See: Tafsir al-Tabari 30/330–331; al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh of al-Baghdadi, pp. 161–162, with commentary. And refer to what precedes: 3/32, note (1).]]
